recipes.name: Spicy Garlic Tofu
instructions: Ensure the tofu is sufficiently pressed before cutting it into ½-inch / 1 cm cubes*.
Place the tofu cubes in a large bowl. Add the cornstarch, salt, and black pepper and gently toss to coat.
In a large skillet, heat the oil over medium-high heat. Cook the tofu for 8 to 10 minutes, until golden. Try to not disturb the tofu too much to avoid crumbling.
Meanwhile, in a small bowl, mix together the maple syrup, gochujang, soy sauce, and rice vinegar. Set aside.

When the tofu is crisped to your liking, transfer it to a plate. In the same pan over medium-high heat, drizzle in the remaining oil. When hot, add the garlic, shallot, chilies, and green onions and cook for about 4 minutes, or until golden.
Reduce the heat to medium and add the sauce, cooking for 2 to 3 minutes, until the sauce becomes sticky.
Add the tofu to the pan and stir to coat.
Transfer to a plate and garnish with some sliced green onions and sesame seeds (if using). Enjoy!

page_recipe_notes: Notes † Gochujang is a Korean fermented red chili paste, which has a sweet, savoury, and spicy flavour profile. It can be found in most Asian supermarkets, but you could also substitute it with another hot sauce, such as Sriracha, if desired. * The more liquid that can be drained, the quicker the tofu cooks and the crispier it gets.
Storage The tofu can be stored in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days.
